newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: George Weston fined for price fixing.
newsitem.headline: George Weston fined for price fixing.

text.p: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Friday that bakery and flour milling group George Weston Foods Ltd had been fined A$1.25 million for fixing the price of bread and attempted resale price maintenance.

The ACCC said it had filed Federal Court proceedings alleging that George Weston, trading as Tip Top Bakeries, had stopped supplying retailers because the retailers were discounting the price of bread.
The incidents occurred at Ferntree Gully in Victoria and at Albury in New South Wales in November 1995, the ACCC said.

"It also admitted having reached an agreement with (the Woolworths Ltd - owned) Safeway to increase the price at which the Tip Top retail store in Preston would sell bread to the public," the ACCC said.
"The company (George Weston) admitted the contraventions and has substantially assisted the ACCC with its investigation from an early stage," the ACCC said.
The ACCC said it had alleged that each of the offences by Tip Top arose out of pressure from Safeway, but that Safeway had denied the allegations.
The Federal Court said in its judgment against George Weston it had taken into account Tip Top's relatively high public profile in the penalty.
ACCC Chairman Allan Fels said the commission was concerned whenever wholesalers or manufacturers try to manipulate prices.
"The ACCC is concerned whenever manufacturers, or wholesalers, try to manipulate retail prices or decide who will, or will not, be able to act competitively," Fels said in a statement.

"This is a case where the rights of small businesses, who were attempting to compete with larger supermarkets, were ignored for the purposes of preserving Tip Top's relationship with larger customers," he said.
"The ACCC will have no hesitation in taking appropriate action should similar circumstances occur in the future."
The ACCC continued to pursue its allegations against Safeway and two of its employees involved in the George Weston incidents and in other incidents involving other bread-makers.
Safeway denied the allegations and a trial is expected within the next six to eight weeks.

An ACCC spokeswoman could not say who the other bread-makers involved were. The ACCC was not prosecuting Safeway's parent, Woolworths, or any of the other bread-makers, the spokeswoman said. George Weston's shares were unchanged at A$8.25.
